summary.text: Luis Sepúlveda is the Democratic nominee for re-election to New York State Senate District 32 in the central Bronx. An attorney, he served three terms in the State Assembly before winning an April 2018 special election to the Senate, where he chairs the Judiciary and Cities 1 committees. He is unopposed in the general election.

paragraphs.text: Sepúlveda was born in Brooklyn on February 11, 1964, according to Wikipedia, and a May 2026 El Diario NY profile reports that he grew up in the Los Sures neighborhood of Brooklyn.

He earned a bachelor's degree and, in 1991, a J.D. from Hofstra University and its Maurice A. Deane School of Law; his official biography describes him as one of two Latinx attorneys in the New York State Legislature.
He worked as an attorney at Community Law Practice and as an adjunct professor at Mercy College.
Sepúlveda lost the 2010 Democratic primary for the 87th Assembly District to incumbent Peter M. Rivera, then won the seat in 2012 after Rivera retired.
He served three terms as Assemblymember for the 87th District (2013-2018), including on the Aging, Agriculture, Banks, Correction, Housing, and Mental Hygiene committees.
In April 2018 he won the special election to the 32nd Senate District, succeeding Rubén Díaz Sr., who left to join the New York City Council.

As a state senator, Sepúlveda helped lead the 2019 criminal-justice reforms ending cash bail for most misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies and establishing new discovery and speedy-trial rules, and he is lead sponsor of the Jose Peralta DREAM Act and the Green Light Law.

On January 12, 2021, he was arrested on a charge of criminal obstruction of breathing after his wife alleged he had choked her during a domestic dispute; he and his wife each accused the other of assault, and his lawyer called her claim false. Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins removed him as chair of the Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and stripped his other committee assignments. The Bronx District Attorney's office dropped all charges on October 4, 2021, stating it could not meet the burden of proof and that his wife did not wish to testify against him.

Sepúlveda chairs the Senate Judiciary Committee (a role Wikipedia dates to January 2026), and El Diario reports he is the first Latino and Puerto Rican to hold that chair. He also chairs the Select Majority Task Force on Diversity in the Judiciary.
According to his official biography, in 2022 he became the first New York State senator granted Dominican citizenship.
